data.long_meaning: The Sanskrit word 'Prithvi' means 'Earth' or 'World'. It is one of the five basic elements of nature and represents the solid, physical world around us. It is also considered as the goddess of the Earth in Hinduism. The name Prithvi carries the meaning “Earth, World” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Prithvi usually hope their child will grow to embody earth, world and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the foundation and stability of life. Represents the connection between the physical world and the divine.
data.etymology: Prithvi belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Earth, World.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Prithvi total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The naming of a child as Prithvi signifies a deep connection to the earth and the natural world. It holds significance in Indian culture as a reminder of our origins and the importance of preserving the natural world for future generations. This name also highlights the Hindu belief in the cyclical nature of life, death, and rebirth, with the Earth serving as the constant.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Prithvi is revered as the goddess of the Earth. She is believed to provide stability, nourishment, and protection. The name Prithvi carries the blessings of the Earth goddess and signifies a strong grounding in spirituality, as well as a respect and appreciation for the natural world. It is also a reminder of the importance of living in harmony with nature.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Prithvi symbolizes the earth element and represents stability, grounding, and nurturing energies. It is the physical realm where life thrives and the foundation for all creation.

historical_references.reference: It is believed that Prithvi, the god of the earth, was the first deity to be worshipped by the early humans. According to Hindu mythology, Prithvi emerged from the cosmic ocean (Samudra Manthan) when churning the ocean with the mount Mandara as the churning rod.
historical_references.context: The early Vedic period, when the ancient Indians began to organize their religious beliefs around various deities.

historical_references.reference: In Hindu mythology, the gods rule from three main domains: the heavens, the earth, and the netherworld. Prithvi, the god of the earth, is the ruler and nurturer of this domain. He is also believed to be the father of all living beings and the source of all existence.
historical_references.context: The later Vedic period, when Hindu mythology became more complex and the gods were given distinct roles and spheres of influence.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Prithvi continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
